plain.li: [ha:line,theirs,!condolences] Hello from the one who actually does the work around here.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] Do not believe a word of the above. Except the nice parts.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,warmly] Send more letters. They are the only thing that keeps this one quiet.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] I am only allowed one line. This is it.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] The goat says hello. The goat has not said this, but I am sure it would.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,warmly] Come and visit. The bed in the corner is free, and only a little lumpy.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] I have read your letters too. I hope that is all right. It is too late now if it is not.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] Tell your cook we want the secret of whatever it is you eat out there.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] The {ANIMALS} are back on the ridge, if anyone over there cares about that sort of thing. I do.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] I tried to draw you a horse for this letter. It came out as a dog. The dog is very good, though.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,warmly] Write back soon. Everyone here argues over who gets to read your letters first.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,w:tribal] Hello from the fire. It is a good fire tonight.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,w:tribal] The small ones drew you a picture in the dirt, but we could not send the dirt.
[ha:line,theirs,condolences] I am so sorry. That is all I wanted to add.
[ha:line,theirs,condolences] We are thinking of you, all of us, every day.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences] Hello from me too.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences] Write back soon. It cheers everyone up.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences] Everything above is true, except the bits about me.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences,warmly] If you are ever passing, there is always room at our table.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences] I have nothing to add, but I did not want to be left out.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences] Say hello to everyone at {TOWN} from me.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences,colony:harvest] The harvest is in, and I helped, and I would like that noted.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences,colony:children] The children want to know whether you have any animals they could name.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences,colony:animals] The animals here send their regards, or they would if they could hold a pen.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences,season:winter] Stay warm out there. We are trying to.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences,season:summer] Keep to the shade. We are, mostly.
[ha:line,ours,condolences] We are all thinking of you.
[ha:line,ours,condolences] I am sorry for your loss. If there is anything at all, ask.
[olde,ha:line,!condolences] I would add my greeting to the rest, and my good wishes to all thy folk.
[olde,ha:line,theirs,!condolences] Believe not a word above, save the kindly parts.
[olde,ha:line,theirs,!condolences,warmly] Come and visit us. There is a bed by the fire, and it is but a little lumpy.
[olde,ha:line,theirs,!condolences] The goat sendeth greeting. The goat hath not said so, but I am sure it would.
[olde,ha:line,ours,!condolences] Commend me to all at {TOWN}.
[olde,ha:line,condolences] We grieve with thee, all of us.
[u:none,ha:line,!condolences] Hello from me too.
[u:none,ha:line,!condolences] Write back, please.
[u:none,ha:line,theirs,!condolences] The goat says hello.
[u:none,ha:line,condolences] We are sorry.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,fam:familiar|fam:close] Tell your writer I have given up trying to read the handwriting and now just enjoy the shapes.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] The cook says there is a plate waiting for anyone from {COLONY}. The cook does not say what is on it.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] I wanted to add a line. Here it is. I had more to say, but somebody needs the pen.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,warmly] Every time a letter comes from you, the evening goes better. Thank you for the evenings.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] I am the youngest, so I get the bottom of the page. Hello. I can write all my letters now.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,fam:close] We have heard so much about you that we feel we have met. We have not. Please fix that.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,fam:new] We do not know you yet, but we know the one writing this, and so we send our greetings too.
[ha:line,theirs,condolences] We are thinking of you, all of us. We do not know what else to put.
[ha:line,theirs,condolences] I did not know your friend. I am sorry all the same, and most of all for you.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,w:tribal] The small one says to tell you she has caught her first fish. She also says it was very big. It was not very big.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,w:tribal] The grandmother says: come and sit at our fire before you are as old as she is.
[ha:line,theirs,condolences,w:tribal] We sang for your dead too. The song is long enough for everyone.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,w:spacer] Adding a line from the next terminal over. Hello. The coffee here is terrible; please send better.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,w:industrial] Written on the back of a work docket, sorry. Hello from the yard.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences] I asked to add a line, and was given one. This is it. Hello from the kitchen.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences,fam:familiar|fam:close] We all read your letters, you know. Some of us more than once. I am one of those.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences] I am not much of a writer, so: hello, and good wishes, and please write back.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences,warmly] Whoever reads this at {TOWN}: you have friends here, even the ones who never write.
[ha:line,ours,condolences] We are sorry, all of us. I am adding my name so you know how many of us are sorry.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences,colony:children] The children want to know if there are children at {TOWN}, and what games they play.
[olde,ha:line,theirs,!condolences] I would add a line. Here it is. I had more, but another wanteth the pen.
[olde,ha:line,theirs,!condolences,fam:familiar|fam:close] Tell thy writer I have given over reading the hand, and do but enjoy the shapes.
[olde,ha:line,theirs,!condolences] I am the youngest, and so have the foot of the page. Greeting. I can write my letters now.
[olde,ha:line,theirs,condolences] We knew not thy friend, yet we grieve with thee, for thy sake.
[olde,ha:line,ours,!condolences] I add my greeting to the rest, and ask that thou write again soon.
[olde,ha:line,ours,condolences] We are sorry, every one of us, and set down our grief beside the rest.
[u:none,ha:line,!condolences] I wrote this bit. It's not much, but it's mine.
[u:none,ha:line,!condolences,fam:familiar|fam:close] I like your letters. The others read them to me.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] The one writing this is too modest to say they stayed up half the night over it. So I am saying it.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences,light] I have been asked to add something clever. I have nothing clever. Hello.
[ha:line,theirs,!condolences] My grandmother says to tell you she remembers when this was all fields. She says this to everyone. It is still all fields.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences,light] Someone has to keep this one honest. I have read the whole letter. Most of it is true.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences] Hello from the one who carries the letters to the gate. I am told that does not count as writing them, but I think it should.
[ha:line,ours,!condolences,colony:animals] The animals here send their regards, through me, since none of them can hold a pen. Some have tried.
[u:none,ha:line,theirs,!condolences] I added this bit myself. My brother holds the pen wrong.
